minutes.headline: Board approved the 30 School Street design RFP, a 15% bag fee increase, and a higher capital threshold
minutes.summary: The board met with the Architectural Preservation District Commission about demolishing the old primary school and discussed ways to memorialize or partly keep it. It then voted on the design services RFP, the capital policy threshold, a constable reappointment, and the trash bag fee increase. It also discussed portable toilet policy, a conservation survey with no cost yet, a 40B application, and the town manager's report, then went into executive session.

what_happened.line: The board voted to approve the request for proposals for landscape architectural and engineering design services at 30 School Street, as modified.
The board passed a 15% increase in the pay-as-you-throw bag fee, without the senior free-bag program.
The board voted to update section 3.02 of the capital budget policy, raising the threshold for what counts as a capital project.
The board met with the Preservation District Commission on the old primary school and asked it to review whether its bylaw allows a retained facade or shell.
The board reappointed a constable, sent portable toilet guidelines to the board of health, and set a 40B workshop for July 27.

why_it_matters: The bag fee vote changes what households pay for trash, and the minutes say the increase from the new contract would have happened regardless of the vote on the senior program.
The 30 School Street RFP starts the design work on the old primary school site, and whether a retained shell is allowed could affect how large that design cost grows.
watch_next: A 40B workshop on the Pond View Commons application is planned for July 27, with comments to the town due by August 9.
The RFP responses for 30 School Street, and the Preservation Commission's review of its bylaw on a retained facade or shell, which was requested before they come back.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the constable, bag-fee and RFP votes and on most named figures, apart from caption mishearings of names and the warrant amounts. The main difference is that our minutes record a vote on the capital policy threshold that the official minutes do not list as a vote, and the threshold figure is garbled in both.
